name: Jose Pierre Adams
notable_stories: Reported by family tradition to be the bastard son of John Quincy Adams, though records indicate Scotland or Virginia birth
He was reportedly accidentally poisoned while testing a variety of herb as a chemist
Immigrated in early manhood (probably the 1810s), settled in Jefferson County, VA
Served as executor of brother-in-law Thomas Hamilton's will in 1836

C-004: RESEARCH FLAG — Jose P. vs Jesse P. name variation. No primary records identified for Jose Pierre Adams. Name may be transcription or naming drift from 'Jesse' to 'Jose'. High-impact uncertainty. Confidence: LOW.
1830 census household: two males 10-15 (likely George and Alexander), one male 40-50 (Jose P.), five girls under 20 and one woman 40-50 (Elizabeth). No census record for him or Elizabeth after 1830.
Per the 1898 biography, he was accidentally poisoned while testing a variety of herb and soon died, aged forty-five.
DPBR: while testing a variety of herb he was accidentally poisoned and soon died, aged forty-five. The author doubts the details but thinks the age may be fairly accurate.
milestones: Settled in Harpers Ferry; worked as a chemist
Served as executor for brother-in-law Thomas Hamilton's will in 1836
Married Elizabeth Eliza Hamilton (1813, Jefferson County, VA)
Census trail: Morgan County VA (1820) → Jefferson County VA (1830)
career: Employed as a chemist in Virginia (per 1898 biography of his grandson)
DPBR: married in Virginia and was employed there as a chemist.
Jose was a member of the Virginia General Assembly; he served one term (1825-1826) in the House of Delegates for Morgan County, per a State Library of Virginia listing.
Jose ran again for the 1826-1827 House of Delegates term for Morgan County but lost.
locations: Bath (now Berkeley Springs), Morgan County, Virginia

Ruled out as his father: Judge Evi Adams (1744–1828) of Wantage, Sussex County, New Jersey, whom about twenty Ancestry member trees give as the father of a "Joseph Perry Adams" married to Elizabeth Hamilton. Evi's church register and his will of 9 Dec 1815 do name a son Joseph, born 15 Mar 1783, but that Joseph stayed in Sussex County: in 1830 a Joseph Adams aged 40–49 headed a household of twelve at Wantage, with nine children under 20, while Jose was in Jefferson County, Virginia. Member trees that follow Evi's son give him wives in Sussex County (1809, and Martha Wisner Post in 1816) and children born there from 1806 to 1837. The "Perry" middle name, Fredericksburg birthplace and English burial in the Hamilton-linked trees have no sources.

1820 census, Bath (Berkeley Springs), Morgan County, Virginia, enumerated 7 Aug 1820, as Joseph P. Adams: one man aged 26–44 (Jose), one man aged 45 or over (unidentified; perhaps a parent or in-law), a woman 26–44 (Elizabeth), a girl 10–15, and two boys and two girls under 10. One person engaged in manufactures, which fits his work as a chemist.

1830 census, Jefferson County, Virginia, as Jose P. Adams: a man and a woman aged 40–49, two boys aged 10–14 (George and Alexander), and five girls: two aged 15–19, one aged 10–14 and two aged 5–9. The two youngest are probably the twins Susan and Ursula.
